sets.title: Luke ISEE Lower — Verbal Reasoning — Set 8
sets.subtitle: ISEE Lower — synonyms & sentence completion

questions.prompt: 1. Sandpaper feels coarse when you rub it. In this sentence, the word COARSE means most nearly —
questions.feedback: A coarse surface like sandpaper is rough to the touch, not smooth or soft.

questions.prompt: 2. The school rules oblige students to wear uniforms. In this sentence, the word OBLIGE means most nearly —
questions.feedback: Rules that oblige students require them to do something; they do not merely allow it.

questions.prompt: 3. The loud thunder perturbed the sleeping baby. In this sentence, the word PERTURB means most nearly —
questions.feedback: To perturb is to disturb or unsettle, the opposite of to calm.

questions.prompt: 4. The word GENEROUS means most nearly —
questions.feedback: A generous person shares freely with others, so unselfish is closest; stingy and greedy are opposites.

questions.prompt: 5. The word STURDY means most nearly —
questions.feedback: Something sturdy is built strongly and does not break easily.

questions.prompt: 6. The word VANISH means most nearly —
questions.feedback: To vanish is to disappear suddenly so it can no longer be seen.

questions.prompt: 7. The word TIMID means most nearly —
questions.feedback: A timid person is shy and easily frightened, not bold.

questions.prompt: 8. The word EXPAND means most nearly —
questions.feedback: To expand is to grow larger or spread out, the opposite of to shrink.

questions.prompt: 9. The word SCARCE means most nearly —
questions.feedback: Something scarce is in short supply and hard to find.

questions.prompt: 10. The word BANISH means most nearly —
questions.feedback: To banish someone is to send them away, often as a punishment.

questions.prompt: 11. The word POLITE means most nearly —
questions.feedback: A polite person is courteous and shows good manners.

questions.prompt: 12. The word RAPID means most nearly —
questions.feedback: Rapid means swift and fast-moving.

questions.prompt: 13. The word ANCIENT means most nearly —
questions.feedback: Ancient things are very old, from a long time ago.

questions.prompt: 14. Unlike his brother, who kept every toy to himself, Sam was ___ and let everyone play with his games.
questions.feedback: The word Unlike signals a contrast: his brother kept things to himself, while Sam shared, so Sam was generous.

questions.prompt: 15. Unlike Mia, who rushed through her work, Zoe was ___ and checked every answer twice.
questions.feedback: Unlike signals a contrast with rushing, so Zoe was careful.

questions.prompt: 16. Because the hikers had no map, they felt ___ in the forest and did not know which way to go.
questions.feedback: Having no map and not knowing which way to go means the hikers felt lost.

questions.prompt: 17. The glass vase is ___, so carry it with both hands and do not drop it.
questions.feedback: A glass vase that must not be dropped is fragile, meaning easily broken.

questions.prompt: 18. After running laps all afternoon, the players were ___ and sat down to rest.
questions.feedback: Running all afternoon left the players weary, meaning very tired.

questions.prompt: 19. The teacher asked the class to ___ in a straight line before leaving the room.
questions.feedback: To assemble in a line is to gather together in an orderly group.

questions.prompt: 20. Ben tried to ___ his little sister by hiding her favorite stuffed animal.
questions.feedback: Hiding her favorite toy would perturb, or upset, his sister — not calm or comfort her.

questions.prompt: 21. The sandpaper felt ___ against the wood, so it could smooth the rough edge.
questions.feedback: Sandpaper works because it feels coarse, meaning rough, against the wood.

questions.prompt: 22. The librarian will ___ the new books on the shelf in alphabetical order.
questions.feedback: Putting books in alphabetical order is arranging them.

questions.prompt: 23. Because the directions were ___, every student knew exactly what to do.
questions.feedback: If every student knew exactly what to do, the directions were clear.

questions.prompt: 24. The shy puppy was ___ and hid behind its owner whenever a stranger came near.
questions.feedback: A puppy that hides from strangers is timid, meaning shy and easily frightened.

questions.prompt: 25. When the bell rang, the students walked ___ to their classrooms without running.
questions.feedback: Walking without running to classrooms is walking calmly.

questions.prompt: 26. The author's final paragraph tried to ___ readers to save water during the dry summer.
questions.feedback: An author who tries to get readers to act is trying to persuade them.

sets.title: Luke ISEE Lower — Quantitative Reasoning — Set 6
sets.subtitle: ISEE Lower — quantitative reasoning

questions.prompt: 1. A square piece of cardboard is 8 inches on each side. A 3-inch square is cut from ONE corner. What is the area of the cardboard that is left?
questions.feedback: The whole square is 8 × 8 = 64 square inches. Cutting out one 3 × 3 corner removes 9, leaving 64 − 9 = 55 square inches.

questions.prompt: 2. A rectangular garden is 12 feet long and 9 feet wide. A rectangular path 4 feet by 3 feet is paved inside it and cannot be planted. What area can be planted?
questions.feedback: The garden is 12 × 9 = 108 square feet. The path takes 4 × 3 = 12, leaving 108 − 12 = 96 square feet.

questions.prompt: 3. A square tile design is 10 inches on each side. A rectangle 6 inches by 4 inches is removed from one corner. What is the area that remains?
questions.feedback: The square is 10 × 10 = 100 square inches. Removing 6 × 4 = 24 leaves 100 − 24 = 76 square inches.

questions.prompt: 4. A triangle flag points to the right at the TOP of a pole. The flag is flipped over a horizontal line. After the flip, the triangle —
options: points to the right at the BOTTOM of the pole
points to the left at the TOP of the pole
points to the left at the BOTTOM of the pole
points to the right at the TOP of the pole
questions.correct: points to the right at the BOTTOM of the pole
questions.feedback: Flipping over a horizontal line turns top and bottom around but not left and right, so the triangle still points right and is now at the bottom.

questions.prompt: 5. An arrow points to the right. The arrow is flipped over a vertical line. After the flip, the arrow —
questions.feedback: Flipping over a vertical line reverses left and right, so a right-pointing arrow points left.

questions.prompt: 6. A sticker is moved from the left side of a page to the right side without turning or flipping it. This change is best described as —
options: It was flipped over a vertical line
It was flipped over a horizontal line
questions.feedback: Moving a shape without turning or flipping it is a slide.

questions.prompt: 7. A teacher packs 84 worksheets in stacks of 7. Which equation shows how to find the number of stacks (s)?
questions.feedback: The total is divided into groups of 7, so s = 84 ÷ 7 = 12 stacks.

questions.prompt: 8. Which expression means '7 less than 3 times a number n'?
questions.feedback: 3 times a number is 3n, and 7 less than that is 3n − 7; 'less than' keeps 3n first.

questions.prompt: 9. Which net folds into a cube?
options: A middle square with one square attached to each of its four sides and one more square attached to one of those side squares
Four squares in a straight row only
A triangle with a square attached to each side
questions.correct: A middle square with one square attached to each of its four sides and one more square attached to one of those side squares
questions.feedback: A cube has 6 square faces. That net has 1 + 4 + 1 = 6 squares arranged so they fold into a closed cube.

questions.prompt: 10. If ♠ × ■ = ♠, and ♠ is not 0, what number must ■ stand for?
questions.feedback: Multiplying by 1 leaves a number unchanged, so ■ must be 1.

questions.prompt: 11. A graph shows a cyclist's distance from home over time. The line climbs steeply, then is flat, then climbs gently. What does the flat part most likely show?
options: The cyclist rode faster and faster
The cyclist turned around and rode home
questions.feedback: On a distance-from-home graph, a flat line means distance is not changing, so the cyclist stopped.

questions.prompt: 12. Look at the pattern: 7, 12, 17, 22, … What is the 10th number in the pattern?
questions.feedback: Each term adds 5. The 10th term is 7 + 9 × 5 = 52.

questions.prompt: 13. One van can carry 9 students. How many vans are needed to carry 74 students?
questions.feedback: 8 vans carry only 72 students, so one more van is needed for the last 2 students: 9 vans in all.

questions.prompt: 14. Use the digits 3, 5, 6, 8, and 9 one time each to build the largest EVEN number. What is the digit in the tens place?
questions.feedback: The largest even number is 98,536 (it must end in 6 or 8, and ending in 6 gives the larger number). Its tens digit is 3.

questions.prompt: 15. A jar holds 6 red, 4 blue, and 2 green marbles. Two red marbles are taken out and replaced with green marbles. How many green marbles are in the jar now?
questions.feedback: The jar started with 2 green marbles and 2 more green marbles were added, so there are 2 + 2 = 4 green marbles.

questions.prompt: 16. Ana is making bags for 8 friends. Each bag gets 5 pencils. Pencils are sold in packs of 10. How could Ana figure out how many packs she needs?
options: Multiply 8 by 5, and then divide by 10
Multiply 10 by 5, and then divide by 8
Divide 8 by 5, and then multiply by 10
Multiply 8 by 10, and then divide by 5
questions.correct: Multiply 8 by 5, and then divide by 10
questions.feedback: First find the total pencils needed: 8 × 5 = 40. Then divide by 10 pencils per pack to get 4 packs. Total first, pack size second.

questions.passage: Sea turtles spend most of their lives in the ocean, but female sea turtles must come ashore to lay their eggs. On a dark night, a female turtle crawls out of the surf and digs a deep nest in the sand with her back flippers. She lays about one hundred eggs, covers them with sand, and returns to the sea. About two months later, the eggs hatch. The tiny turtles dig their way up through the sand, usually at night, and hurry toward the water. Bright lights from houses and streets can confuse the hatchlings and lead them away from the ocean, so many beach towns ask people to turn off outdoor lights during hatching season.

questions.passage: For hundreds of years, lighthouses have helped ships travel safely along rocky coasts. Before modern navigation tools, a ship's captain could not always tell where the shore was on a dark or foggy night. A lighthouse's bright beam warned sailors about dangerous rocks and showed them the way into a harbor. Early lighthouses burned wood or oil lamps. Later, strong electric lights and lenses that focused the beam let the light be seen from far away. Today, most lighthouses are controlled by computers and no longer need a keeper living in them, but sailors still value them as a backup when electronic systems fail.

Electric lights were invented for lighthouses

questions.feedback: The whole passage describes how lighthouses warned and guided ships in the past and why sailors still value them now.

sets.title: Luke ISEE Lower — Mathematics Achievement — Set 7
sets.subtitle: ISEE Lower — mathematics achievement

questions.prompt: 1. A number line runs from 0 to 24 and is divided into 6 equal spaces. Each space is worth 4. What number is at the 3rd mark after 0?
questions.feedback: There are 6 equal spaces across 24, so each space is 24 ÷ 6 = 4. The 3rd mark is 3 × 4 = 12, not the number of spaces times something else.

questions.prompt: 2. A number line is marked in steps of 3. Point P sits 4 marks to the LEFT of 0. What number is at P?
questions.feedback: Moving left from 0 goes negative. Each mark is 3, so 4 marks left is 0 − 4 × 3 = −12.

questions.prompt: 3. A thermometer number line is marked in steps of 2. Point Q sits 3 marks to the LEFT of 4. What number is at Q?
questions.feedback: Start at 4 and move 3 marks of 2 to the left: 4 − 3 × 2 = 4 − 6 = −2.
Use twelfths: 5/6 = 10/12 and 1/4 = 3/12, so the sum is 13/12 = 1 1/12.

questions.prompt: 7. After a 20% discount, a jacket costs $56. What was the original price?
questions.feedback: After 20% off you pay 80% of the original. $56 ÷ 0.8 = $70. Check: 20% of $70 is $14, and $70 − $14 = $56.

questions.prompt: 8. Which fraction is the greatest?
questions.feedback: Compare in twenty-fourths/eighths: 7/8 = 0.875, 5/6 ≈ 0.833, 3/4 = 0.75, 4/5 = 0.8, so 7/8 is greatest.

questions.prompt: 9. How many centimeters are in 2.5 meters?
questions.feedback: One meter is 100 centimeters, so 2.5 × 100 = 250 centimeters.

questions.prompt: 10. A square has a side of 6 inches. Which statement is TRUE?
options: It is also a rectangle, and all four of its angles are right angles
It is not a rectangle because its sides are equal
Its angles add up to 180 degrees
It has only two right angles
questions.correct: It is also a rectangle, and all four of its angles are right angles
questions.feedback: A square meets the definition of a rectangle (four right angles, opposite sides equal) and all four of its angles are right angles.

questions.prompt: 11. What is the next number in the pattern 2, 6, 12, 20, 30, …?
questions.feedback: The gaps grow: +4, +6, +8, +10, so the next gap is +12 and 30 + 12 = 42.

questions.prompt: 12. Mia scored 72, 84, and 90 on three tests. What must she score on a fourth test to have an average of 84?
questions.feedback: An average of 84 over 4 tests needs a total of 336. She has 72 + 84 + 90 = 246, so she needs 336 − 246 = 90.

questions.prompt: 13. What is 0.45 written as a percent?
questions.feedback: To write a decimal as a percent, multiply by 100: 0.45 × 100 = 45%.

questions.prompt: 14. A recipe calls for 3/4 cup of sugar for one batch. How much sugar is needed for 4 batches?
questions.feedback: Multiply: 4 × 3/4 = 12/4 = 3 cups.

questions.prompt: 15. Which expression is equal to 48 ÷ (6 × 2)?
questions.feedback: Do the parentheses first: 6 × 2 = 12, and 48 ÷ 12 = 4.
